name: Kerabond T
description: Kerabond T is the C1T adhesive in the Mapei cementitious range, a grey or white powder with high grab and no vertical slip, so wall tiles can be set from the top down without spacer pegs. Where it stops is the useful part. Mapei keeps it to absorbent ceramic and mosaic over sound render, well aged concrete or primed gypsum, and rules it out for non-absorbent tiles over non-absorbent substrates, wood and plasterboard, and floors needing quick foot traffic. Porcelain, large formats, tile over tile, heated screeds and external work belong to a C2 such as Keraflex, or to Kerabond T gauged with Isolastic. Consumption follows the trowel: 2 to 3 kg per square metre on a No. 4 or 5, 4 to 5 kg on a No. 5 or 6, over 6 kg for large sizes and exteriors. Tiles adjust for 45 minutes; floors grout at 24 hours.

name: Keraflex Maxi S1 Zero
description: Keraflex Maxi S1 Zero is the thick bed member of the Mapei deformable adhesive family, classified C2TE S1, the deformable grade for large and heavy tiles. Bed depth is the honest distinction against plain Keraflex: this one holds its shape at high thickness, so a large format slab does not sink into the mortar on a floor or slide down a wall as it sets. Against a C1 adhesive such as Kerabond T, the C2 grip plus deformability is what carries porcelain and stone over heated screeds, waterproofed surfaces and existing tiles. Open time runs beyond 30 minutes and a tile is still adjustable at roughly 45 minutes, which is the figure that counts on a UAE site where application is allowed up to 40 degrees. Grey and white, 25 kg bags, EC1 Plus rated.

name: Mapeset
description: Mapeset is a fast setting, cementitious tile adhesive from Mapei, classified C1 under EN 12004 and ISO 13007-1. It is formulated for bonding ceramic tiles and mosaics on floors, walls and ceilings, indoors and outdoors. The mix stays workable for 6 to 8 hours, holds tiles with no appreciable shrinkage and reaches light foot traffic in about 24 hours, which suits time sensitive fixing schedules on UAE sites. Typical substrates include traditional render, cement mortar and cured cementitious screeds, with gypsum and anhydrite surfaces possible after priming. Consumption runs from about 2 kg per square metre for mosaics up to 5 kg per square metre for external floors. Mapeset is produced in white and grey and supplied in 25 kg bags. name: Kerapoxy Adhesive
description: Kerapoxy Adhesive is a two component epoxy adhesive from Mapei, classified R2T under EN 12004, an improved reactive adhesive with no vertical slip. It bonds ceramic, porcelain and stone on floors and walls over practically any substrate used in construction, achieving a rigid, chemical resistant, high strength connection. Typical uses include bullnose and special ceramic shapes, tiles in fibreglass swimming pools, and marble doorsteps and windowsills, where cementitious adhesives either cannot grip or cannot deliver the required durability. The thixotropic consistency holds pieces in position on vertical surfaces while curing. For UAE fit outs involving chemically aggressive environments or non standard substrates, Kerapoxy Adhesive provides a dependable specification. Download the full technical data sheet on this page for pot life, hardening times and consumption data.

name: Kerapoxy Easy Design
description: Kerapoxy Easy Design is a two component, decorative, acid resistant epoxy grout from Mapei, classified RG under EN 13888 and R2T as an adhesive. It was developed to make epoxy grouting genuinely easy to apply and clean off, with a smooth creamy texture that fills joints in ceramic, glass mosaic and stone with a fine, uniform finish. A bacteriostatic agent with BioBlock technology helps joints stay hygienic in wet and humid conditions. It suits decorative grouting of internal and external floors and walls and also provides an acid resistant bond on common building substrates. For designers in the UAE it opens a wide palette of colours that keep their appearance under regular cleaning. The full technical data sheet with times, consumption and chemical resistance is available for download here.

name: Kerapoxy
description: Kerapoxy is a two component, acid resistant epoxy mortar from Mapei, classified RG under EN 13888 as a grout and R2T as an adhesive. It grouts joints of at least 1 mm in ceramic tile and natural stone floors and walls, indoors and outdoors, and can also be used for acid resistant bonding of tiles, stone, fibre cement and concrete. Cured Kerapoxy resists chemicals, stains and frequent aggressive cleaning, and supports installations that must comply with HACCP food safety requirements. That makes it the reference choice for commercial kitchens, food production areas, laboratories, swimming pools and industrial floors across the UAE. Available in 17 colours. name: Mapegrout T60 ME
description: Mapegrout T60 ME is a thixotropic, fibre reinforced structural repair mortar classified R4 under EN 1504-3, applied to concrete that has already deteriorated rather than added to a fresh mix. Thixotropic means hand applied: it is trowelled or sprayed onto vertical surfaces in layers up to 60 mm thick and overhead in layers up to 30 mm, with no formwork, from a minimum of 10 mm. Where a section is deeper, or the reinforcement too congested for mortar to be worked in behind the bars, a flowable micro concrete poured into formwork is the correct answer instead. Sulphate and chloride resistance is why it suits marine structures, sewerage, tunnels and water retaining works, and the UAE coastal and groundwater conditions that drove the corrosion in the first place. Pot life is about an hour, applied between 5 and 50 degrees.

It grouts floors and walls in every type of ceramic, terracotta, stone and glass or marble mosaic, is walkable after roughly 24 hours and never produces efflorescence. Deformability class S1 helps the adhesive absorb substrate movement, which suits large format tiles and demanding commercial floors. name: Keralastic
description: Keralastic is a two component polyurethane adhesive from Mapei, classified R2 under EN 12004, for bonding ceramic tiles, stone material and mosaics where cementitious products reach their limits. Being reaction cured, it adheres to screeds, renders and concrete as well as difficult substrates such as wood, metal, PVC, reinforced polyester, fibre cement and gypsum board. It contains no water or solvents, cures without shrinkage and forms a tough, flexible bond that copes with substrate movement. Typical uses include showers, prefabricated bathroom sheets, wooden worktops and mixed substrate refurbishments. For UAE projects involving unusual substrates or wet areas, Keralastic offers a dependable reactive alternative to cement based adhesives. description: Mixed in place of water, Isolastic turns an ordinary Mapei cementitious adhesive into a deformable one. Mapei states that Kerabond T, a C1T bag on its own, reaches class C2ES2 when gauged with this latex rather than water, so the real decision is whether to stock one adhesive plus an additive or several pre-blended grades. The additive route suits a mixed specification: full strength for heavy stone and movement, diluted one part to one with water for lighter work, plain water for straightforward ceramic. Working figures follow the adhesive, with open time of 20 to 30 minutes, around 45 minutes to adjust a tile and wall joints ready for grouting after 4 to 8 hours. A pinkish white liquid in 5 and 25 kg tanks, usable from 5 to 40 degrees, stable for 24 months.

description: Planicrete SP is a multipurpose latex additive for mortars and a component of cementitious mortar adhesives, which places it with the mix modifiers and not with the repair or sealing ranges. name: Mapecolor Metallic
description: What this one changes is appearance, not performance. Mapecolor Metallic is a powder pigment based on very high quality pearlescent mica, dosed into mixed Kerapoxy Easy Design epoxy grout at up to 3 per cent by weight, which is exactly what one 90 g sachet gives on a 3 kg drum. Five tones are offered, Moonlight like platinum, Sahara like gold, Shining like silver, Red Clay like copper and Stardust like dark silver, and the most even result comes off the translucent Kerapoxy Easy Design 700 base. Go over the dose and the workability of the grout suffers. The powder is extremely fine and volatile, so Mapei asks for it to be blended outdoors in a spot sheltered from draughts, which on a UAE site means a screened bay, and the mix used within 45 minutes.

name: Porcelain Plus Green
description: Porcelain Plus Green is a premixed deformable tile adhesive classified C2TES1, formulated for porcelain slabs and large format tiles while carrying a lower embodied carbon than a conventional cementitious adhesive. Porcelain absorbs almost nothing, so the bond is mechanical rather than suction driven, and the S1 deformability absorbs the movement a large tile transmits as it expands and contracts. The same bed suits marble, granite, mosaic and ceramic, which makes it a practical single adhesive on a mixed specification. Ordinary line marking paint on a car park deck fades, chalks and is worn off by tyres within a season; a two component polyurethane cures to a hard film that survives both the traffic and the sunlight. It is used for line marking over the Vetotop range and car park deck coating systems, over general epoxy and polyurethane coated decks, and on car park flooring. UV resistance is what keeps the colour legible rather than bleached, which matters when the lines are doing a safety job. Supplied as a 4 litre kit, a size that suits the volumes line marking actually uses. Clean tools with Vetonit Solvent XX300 before the coating cures.

name: Vetotop US172
description: Vetotop US172 is a three component heavy duty polyurethane hybrid flooring system, the specification for floors facing mechanical and chemical attack at the same time. Its natural home is food and beverage production: dairies, cheese and milk production, meat, fish and poultry processing, along with laboratories and general factory floors. Those environments combine hot washdown, aggressive cleaning chemicals, organic acids and constant wheeled traffic, a set of conditions that will lift an epoxy through thermal shock alone. A polyurethane hybrid tolerates the temperature swing while keeping the chemical resistance and the seamless hygienic finish. Supplied as a 30 kg kit of resin, hardener and filler mixed on site, with tools cleaned in Vetonit Solvent XX300 before cure. Specify the finish and slip resistance before ordering, not after.

name: Vetoprime Décor
description: Vetoprime Decor is a single component pure acrylic penetrating primer, supplied ready to use, that prepares a surface before a decorative finish goes on. It penetrates rather than forming a film, which is what suits it to porous and slightly chalky substrates where a surface film would simply peel away with the dust it is sitting on. It primes concrete, masonry and plaster for interior and exterior use, and is the specified primer beneath the Vetotouch Decor decorative range. Priming matters more on a decorative finish than on anything else, because an uneven substrate suction shows as a patchy colour in the finish coat and cannot be corrected afterwards without taking it off. name: Vetonit Putty WR
description: Vetonit Putty WR is a water resistant premixed cementitious putty, the skim coat that gives a wall its final smooth surface before paint. Being cement based rather than a filler, it survives the damp that would break down an internal putty, which is what the WR designation marks. It is applied over plaster, concrete and blockwork to take out the fine texture a render leaves, and it is the layer that decides whether a painted wall reads as flat or shows every trowel mark under raking light. Consumption is 1.1 kg per square metre per millimetre of thickness. A 25 kg bag takes 10 to 11 litres of clean water, and a 40 kg bag 16 to 17.6 litres. Wet the wall before applying, as the sheet instructs.

description: Putty Fine is a PVA based ready to use finishing putty for internal walls and ceilings, supplied in 20 kg pails so there is no mixing and no water ratio to judge. name: Vetonit Gypsum Joint Compound
description: Vetonit Gypsum Joint Compound is a premixed powder for jointing and finishing gypsum board, applied from 1 to 5 mm. Board jointing is its own discipline: the compound has to fill the recess, bed the tape, and feather out far enough either side that the joint disappears under paint, without shrinking back and leaving the tape edge visible. A compound formulated for the job does that; a general filler does not. It also levels minor surface undulations and works as a smooth skimming compound, and is used internally on both horizontal and vertical surfaces, which matters because ceiling work is where a heavy compound becomes unworkable. A 20 kg bag takes 7.5 to 8.8 litres of clean water. Build in the coats the sheet specifies rather than one thick pass.

description: Vetogyps Compound is a multipurpose ready to use drywall joint compound supplied in 28 kg pails, mixed and ready to open. name: Vetonit Crack Filler
description: Vetonit Crack Filler is a premixed cementitious filler for static cracks up to 4 mm, blowholes and minor surface undulations. The word static is the specification: a crack that is still moving will reopen through any filler, so the cause has to be addressed first and a movement joint formed if that is what the structure needs. Within that limit it does the making good that lets a wall take paint or a coating cleanly, filling the blowholes and hairline cracking that a render or a concrete pour leaves behind. It works internally and externally in wet and dry conditions, which is more than a gypsum based filler can claim. A 20 kg bag takes 7 to 8 litres of clean water. Open the crack out slightly before filling so the material has something to hold.

description: Vetorel XT420 is a water based mould and formwork release agent, applied to wooden and metal shuttering before concrete is cast so the form strips cleanly. A release agent does more than save labour at striking: it minimises surface blemishes, blowholes and staining on the finished concrete, which matters a great deal on fair faced work where the concrete is the finish and there is no second chance. Apply thinly and evenly: excess release agent is as damaging to the surface as too little, and it can interfere with anything applied afterwards.

name: Vetotard XT428
description: Vetotard XT428 is a water based surface retarder, used to produce exposed aggregate concrete by delaying the set of the cement paste at the surface only. Once the body of the concrete has hardened, the retarded skin is washed off to reveal the aggregate beneath, which is how an exposed aggregate finish is actually made rather than by grinding. It is used for exposed aggregate concrete and precast panels, in both face down and face up pours, and to leave a deliberately rough surface where a later layer has to bond to it. Supplied ready to use in 20 litre pails. Timing governs the result: wash off too early and the aggregate is undermined, too late and the retarded layer has set. Trial panels are the usual way to fix the window.

name: Vetoseal XW770
description: Vetoseal XW770 is a silicone based polymeric water repellent, pore sealer and hardener for limestone, masonry and natural stone. It penetrates into the pore structure and lines it rather than forming a film across the face, so the substrate still breathes and trapped moisture can escape, while liquid water is shed. A film forming sealer on stone traps moisture behind it and eventually blows the surface off. It works as a universal limestone and masonry sealer and hardener, strengthens weak limestone and masonry facades, and acts as a dust proofer on cementitious surfaces. Supplied ready to use in 20 litre containers. The substrate must be dry and free of construction moisture before application, and a test area is worth doing because some stones darken slightly.

name: Vetoseal XW771
description: Vetoseal XW771 is a water based silane siloxane water repellent, used to turn an absorbent construction surface into one that sheds water. name: Vetogrout CG510
description: Vetogrout CG510 is a single component multipurpose non shrink cementitious grout, placed from 5 to 50 mm. It grouts and anchors structural steel and precast concrete members, fills voids and tie rod holes, and handles under plate grouting and light machine beds. For a statically loaded base plate this is the standard specification; where the load is dynamic, an epoxy grout is the right answer instead. Supplied as a dry powder in 25 kg bags needing only clean water, which keeps site mixing simple on a pour that has to be continuous. Twelve month shelf life in sealed bags stored dry.

name: Vetogrout EG340
description: Vetogrout EG340 is a three component epoxy grout formulated for dynamic loads, and that is the distinction that matters when choosing between it and a cementitious grout. A cementitious grout carries a static load well and breaks down under vibration and impact; an epoxy grout carries both. It grouts and anchors bridge bearings and pile caps, handles under plate grouting and heavy machine beds, and suits industrial applications needing chemical resistance and rapid strength development. It is also waterproof, which matters where the grout line sits in a wet or buried location. Supplied as a 30 kg kit of resin, hardener and graded filler, mixed on site in the stated proportions. The working time starts when the parts meet, so plan a continuous pour before mixing anything.

name: Vetogrout ER717
description: Vetogrout ER717 is a two component low viscosity epoxy injection resin, used to restore the structural integrity of cracked concrete rather than to cosmetically hide the crack. It is injected into retaining walls, beams, columns, shear walls and tanks, and used for grouting and static crack filling. The word static matters: injecting a crack that is still moving bonds the two faces and the structure simply cracks again alongside the repair, so the cause has to be dealt with first. Supplied as a 4 litre kit mixed on site in the stated ratio, placed through injection ports rather than poured.

description: Once a hardwood floor is laid and sanded it still has to be protected, and Aqua-Pur Basic is the base coat in that final layer. description: Not every defect in a timber floor can be sanded away. description: Aquastop AR1 is a reinforcing mesh of alkali resistant glass fibre. Lap the mesh as the data sheet requires and work it fully into the first coat, since mesh left sitting on the surface reinforces nothing.

description: Aquastop BT is a self adhesive butyl tape, which separates it from an NBR joint bedded into adhesive. It forms the screed layer over the structural slab, levelling it and carrying the adhesive and covering above. Ready to use earns its cost on a fit out, because it takes site batching out as a variable, and a screed mixed by eye varies in strength from one gang to the next. The phrase worth noting is covered with adhesives: this is a screed to bond a covering onto, not a wearing surface in itself. Supplied in 25 kg bags with a 3 hour pot life and a 12 month shelf life. Rapid drying is what shortens the wait before a covering can go down in a humid coastal climate.

name: Keracem Prontoplus
description: Keracem Prontoplus is the fibre reinforced member of the Keracem family, a certified ready to use, normal setting and rapid drying mineral screed to be covered with adhesives. It occupies the same layer as Keracem Pronto, between the structural slab and the floor covering, and the fibres are the reason to choose it: dispersed reinforcement controls the fine shrinkage cracking a screed is prone to across large bays and over services. If the screed will be thin, heated or broken up by a complicated floor plan, that matters. The pot life is 2 hours, an hour shorter than Pronto, so plan the pour in smaller sections. Supplied in 25 kg bags with a 12 month shelf life. Protect a fresh screed from direct sun and site draughts, which in the Emirates dry the surface long before the body has cured.

name: Keradur
description: Keradur is applied before anything else in the build up. It is a certified water based deep consolidant for absorbent substrates, and consolidating is a different job from priming: a primer conditions a surface for the next coat, while a consolidant penetrates a weak, friable or dusty substrate and binds it back together so there is something sound to build on. Use it where a screed is chalky, over sanded or simply old and a primer alone would sit on loose material. If the substrate is already sound, a primer is the cheaper and correct choice. Supplied in 5 kg cans with a 12 month shelf life. On refurbishment work in the Emirates, old screeds under lifted tiles are often weaker than they look once the bed has been ground off, so test the surface before deciding which route to take.

name: Keragrip Pulep
description: Non absorbent substrates are the awkward case in flooring, and Keragrip Pulep is made for them: an organic preparation coat for the treatment and cleaning of surfaces that will not take water in. Existing ceramic, resin and other sealed floors give an adhesive nothing to key into, and they usually carry a film of polish, oil or release agent as well. This product treats and cleans that surface so the layer above can bond, which puts it at the preparation step, below any primer or adhesive. A water drop decides it: if the substrate absorbs, use a consolidant or a primer instead. Supplied in 10 litre drums with a 12 month shelf life. Overlaying rather than removing an existing tiled floor is common on UAE fit outs, and this is the step that makes the overlay dependable.

name: Keraplast P6
description: Keraplast P6 is a latex for mineral mortars and slurry keys, added to the mixing water rather than applied as a layer of its own. Its job is adhesion and cohesion. A slurry key gauged with latex grips a smooth dense substrate that a plain cement slurry would simply sit on, and a mineral mortar modified with it bonds better to the surrounding material. Because it changes the mortar rather than coating the wall, the dose follows the mortar being modified, so take it from the data sheet for the mix being gauged rather than by eye. Supplied in 1 kg cans with twelve months of shelf life, a size that suits site repairs and small areas. On a hot UAE site, latex gauged mixes stiffen quickly, so gauge only what the gang can place.

name: Kerarep
description: Kerarep is a repair product rather than a layer of its own: an extra fast acting bonding agent for gaps and cracks, used to stabilise a substrate before the floor goes over it. Cracks and open joints in a screed do not stay where they are once a covering is bonded across them, so they are either filled and bonded or they come back through the finish. Extra fast acting is the point, because this work falls in the gap between preparation and laying, and a product that needs a day to cure stops the whole sequence. Reach for it on localised faults, since a generally weak screed needs a consolidant instead. The shelf life is 18 months, longer than most of this range, so it is practical to keep a container on the van for cracks nobody saw until the old covering came up.

name: L34 Evolution
description: L34 Evolution is the adhesive layer under a glued down hardwood floor, specified by Kerakoll as an odourless, two component organic mineral adhesive for high performance laying. Two components mean a reactive cure that does not depend on water leaving the adhesive, which is what lets hardwood be bonded over substrates and in board thicknesses where a water based adhesive would move the timber. Odourless is the practical differentiator: a hardwood floor is often laid late in a fit out, in a building that is already partly occupied, and odour decides whether that is possible at all. The pot life and open time are both 90 minutes, so a mixed batch and a spread bed give the same working window. It has a 12 month shelf life. Acclimatise the boards in the conditioned space before laying, never in a hot store.

Elastic is the characteristic that matters: the cured bond flexes, so it takes up movement between the boards and what they are fixed to instead of cracking along the joint. Use it for detail work, perimeters, repairs and fixings a trowelled bed cannot reach. The open time is 60 minutes and the shelf life is 12 months. Keep cartridges out of the sun on site, because a cartridge left on a hot slab in the Emirates will be stiff enough to be unusable by the time the fitter needs it.

name: L34 Hybrid
description: Single component is the distinction that defines L34 Hybrid, an organic mineral adhesive for the high performance laying of hardwood floors. There is nothing to mix, so there is no ratio to get wrong and no mixed batch wasted if the day stops early, which is why a single component adhesive is often chosen for smaller areas and for work that proceeds in stages. It still occupies the same layer as the two component grades, bonding boards to the prepared substrate. The open time is 60 minutes, shorter than the mixed L34 adhesives, so spread the bed in sections the fitter can stay ahead of. Supplied in 16 kg buckets with a 12 month shelf life. name: Metric Osmotic
description: Osmotic waterproofing works through the concrete rather than on top of it, and Metric Osmotic is the cement based version Kerakoll supplies for that purpose. It is applied as a waterproofing and protective product to concrete, and because the action is osmotic it suits structures where water pushes from the far face and a surface film would simply be driven off, so tanks, basements and lift pits. Classification is EN 1504-2, the standard for concrete surface protection, which is the line a consultant looks for on a repair specification. Supplied in 25 kg bags, with a pot life of one hour and a shelf life of 12 months. This is a concrete protection product, so it belongs with the structural repair materials on a job rather than with the under tile Aquastop system.

name: Nanodefense
description: Nanodefense is a certified, organic, water based waterproofing product for absorbent substrates in damp environments, and the words to notice are absorbent and water based. Being water based it is low odour and simple to clean up, which makes it workable inside occupied buildings; being formulated for absorbent substrates it is aimed at plaster, screed and board rather than dense or non porous surfaces. It is a liquid membrane for the field of the surface, so corners and floor to wall joints still want an Aquastop tape, which is where leaks in UAE wet rooms usually begin.

name: Neutro Color
description: Neutro Color is a decorative sealant intended for marble and natural stone. The distinction matters, because marble and other calcareous stones can be stained at the edge of a joint by the wrong sealant, which bleeds oils into the stone and leaves a dark halo that will not clean off. A sealant formulated for stone avoids that, and the colour range lets a movement joint read as part of the finish rather than a line through it. Supplied in 310 ml cartridges with an 18 month shelf life, shorter than the silicone products in the same range, so order to the quantity actually needed. Use it on the joints a stone floor needs, at perimeters, at changes of plane and over structural movement joints, and keep grout for everything in between.

name: Pragma Easy
description: Pragma Easy is the entry point of the Pragma mineral adhesives, classified C1 E. C1 marks normal rather than improved adhesion, which suits absorbent ceramic tiles that draw water from the bed as the bond forms, and makes it the economical answer for standard ceramic work. It is the wrong choice under porcelain, which absorbs almost nothing and needs a C2 grade. The E is extended open time, stated at 30 minutes, and that is the practical benefit on a large floor where a standard adhesive skins over before the tiler gets back to it. Supplied in 25 kg bags with a pot life of 4 hours and a 12 month shelf life. Store the bags off the floor and away from humidity, because a mineral adhesive that has taken up moisture will not reach its stated strength.

name: Quarzo
description: Quarzo is not a layer by itself but the aggregate that makes other layers work: calibrated mineral quartz of controlled granulometry, washed and perfectly dry. Controlled grading and dryness are exactly what site sand does not offer, and both matter, because a filler of known particle size is what gives a primer or resin coat its texture, its build and its stability. It is broadcast into a primer to key the next layer, blended into mortars and resins where a filler is specified, and used wherever a clean dry quartz is called for in the build up. The decision is straightforward: where a data sheet specifies a graded quartz, local sand is not a substitute. Supplied in 25 kg bags. Keep bags sealed and off the ground on site, since damp quartz defeats the one property it was bought for.

description: Biocalce Rinzaffo is a WTA certified breathable mortar based on NHL 3.5 natural hydraulic lime, used as the rough coat that goes on before a dehumidifying plaster. name: Mapefer

description: Mapetard RCC ME is a liquid retarding admixture with a plasticising effect, used to hold a cementitious mix workable rather than to speed anything up. It conforms to ASTM C494. Supplied in bulk, in 1000 litre IBCs and in 25 kg jerrycans, with a two year shelf life in closed containers kept above 5 degrees and out of direct sunlight. Heat shortens the working life of every cementitious mix, so on a UAE site this admixture is doing in reverse exactly what the weather does, and it earns its place in summer grouting.

name: Mapewrap 21
description: MapeWrap 21 is a two component, super fluid epoxy resin used to impregnate MapeWrap fabrics immediately before they are placed on concrete, reinforced concrete or masonry for repair or strengthening. It belongs to the composite strengthening system rather than to the mortar or sealant ranges: the fabric carries the load, and the resin saturates it and bonds it to the prepared substrate. Super fluid consistency is what makes it the damp system resin, with the fabric wetted out as it goes on. Adhesion to concrete exceeds 3 N per square millimetre after 7 days at 23 degrees, with failure occurring in the concrete rather than at the bond line. The working range is 10 to 30 degrees, which on a UAE facade usually means early morning work. Supplied in 5 kg units with a 24 month shelf life.

name: Monofinish
description: Smoothing rather than structural repair is what Monofinish is for: a one component, normal setting cementitious mortar trowelled onto concrete and cement render at a maximum of 2 to 3 mm per coat. name: Planicrete
description: Planicrete is a synthetic rubber latex gauged into cement mixes to improve their adhesion and mechanical performance, so it modifies a mortar rather than being one. It is used as an admixture in cement based screeds, renders and thin smoothing layers, and in highly adhesive cement bonding slurries. Typical work includes high strength screeds and renders inside and out, bonding slurries that let a new screed hold onto an existing one, cementitious slurry for laying natural stone with the Mapestone system, adhesive shotcrete for bonding renders, and mortars for filling holes and finishing precast elements. It is applied between 5 and 40 degrees, supplied in 25 kg and 5 kg containers, and keeps for 24 months unopened. Where the finished surface takes abrasion, such as a ramp or a channel, the latex earns its cost several times over.

description: Planitop 105 ME is a one component cementitious blowhole filler and levelling mortar, classified R2, built up to 3 mm in as many layers as a smooth finish needs. name: Mapelux Lucida
description: The last layer of a floor build up is the one that gets renewed. Mapelux Lucida is a cross linked high strength metallic wax with a shiny finish, applied at 50 g/m² as part of routine cleaning and maintenance rather than as part of the floor itself. A sacrificial wax takes the scuffing and the cleaning chemicals so the resin or cementitious surface beneath it does not, and it is stripped and reapplied on a cycle instead of being repaired. Cross linking is what gives it enough strength to be worth applying on a commercial floor at all. It is applied between +10°C and +30°C and supplied in 10 kg units with a 12 month shelf life. For a UAE retail unit, set the renewal cycle against footfall, not the calendar.

name: Mapesilent
description: Acoustic failure between apartments is usually structural contact rather than a thin floor. Mapesilent Panel is a dry soundproofing tile one metre square and 13 mm thick, a bitumen and polymer elastoplastomeric membrane sandwiched with polyester fibre, laid fibre side down on the slab and screeded over. It belongs between the structure and the floating screed, never directly under the covering, where Mapesonic CR is the right product instead. Joints are sealed with Mapesilent Tape and the perimeter with Mapesilent Band R so that no acoustic bridge survives. Estimated footstep noise reduction is 31.1 dB, with up to 42.0 dB measured on site, and thermal resistance adds 0.313 m²K/W. A pallet of 75 tiles covers 75 m². Store out of direct sunlight, which on a UAE site rules out the open yard.

name: Ultrabond P980 1K
description: One component adhesives remove the mixing error, and for laminate that matters more than raw strength. Ultrabond P980 1K is a ready mixed one component polyurethane adhesive for engineered laminated parquet, pre assembled panels and laminate on all types of substrate, with no solvent, free amine or epoxy resin content and an EC1 Plus emission classification. It is spread at 800 to 1,000 g/m² and particularly recommended over heated sublayers. Working times are long for a reactive adhesive: a skin forms at 110 minutes, boards can be adjusted for three hours and the floor sets in about 12 hours. The application range is +10°C to +25°C, narrower than most of this range and the one UAE detail to plan around, because the air conditioning has to be running before the first board goes down.

Maximum permitted movement in service is 12.5 per cent, so it is a sanitary and glazing sealant rather than a structural movement joint product, and it is not for traffic. Typical work is bathrooms, kitchens, laundry rooms, baths, showers and saunas, greenhouses, U profile glass, joints between glass and window frames, and air and water vents. Skin forms in 25 minutes, Shore A hardness is 18 and cartridges hold 280 ml.

name: Ultrabond 575
description: Ultrabond 575 is a water dispersion adhesive with a strong, rapid initial hold, used in interiors to bond skirtings and profiles in rigid PVC, rubber, wood and carpet onto absorbent wall substrates. It is solvent free, certified GEV EC1, resistant to water once set, and does not stain or mark light coloured skirting. name: Eco Prim T Plus
description: Priming is the step most often skipped on a floor and most often the reason the levelling layer above it debonds. Eco Prim T Plus is a universal acrylic primer that works on absorbent and non-absorbent substrates alike, which is unusual: it regulates suction on a porous screed so the compound keeps its own mixing water, and it promotes adhesion on dense or already sealed surfaces where a cementitious compound has nothing to grip. It also fixes light dust and isolates gypsum from cement. Supplied as a fluid light blue liquid in 20 kg packs, consumption runs from 30 to 150 g/m² depending on the porosity of the substrate and how it is applied, between +5°C and +35°C. On UAE sites the power floated slab is the usual case, and that is precisely the surface a compound will not bond to unprimed.

name: Primer G
description: Primer G is a synthetic resin primer in water dispersion, and what it does explains why no levelling layer should be poured without one. It evens out the absorption of the substrate so the compound above does not lose its mixing water into the slab and cure weak and dusty, it binds residual dust, and on gypsum or anhydrite it forms a film that prevents the sulphate reaction with cement which otherwise separates the two layers. Use it before smoothing compounds on cementitious, anhydrite and gypsum surfaces, and between coats of smoothing compound once the first is dry. Supplied as a light blue liquid in 25 kg and 5 kg packs, consumption is 0.08 to 0.15 kg/m² depending on porosity, applied from +5°C to +35°C. description: Rust is the only stain this bottle is for. name: Antipluviol
description: Antipluviol is an impregnating water repellent rather than a membrane, and that distinction decides where it belongs. Water based and transparent, it soaks into very absorbent masonry and leaves a hydrophobic barrier inside the pores, so driving rain is shed while the wall still breathes and looks unchanged. Exposed brickwork, aerated concrete, renders, skim coats and natural or artificial stone are its substrates, which makes it a facade product and not something for a tank or a buried wall. Consumption follows absorbency, roughly 0.2 to 1 litre per square metre, with render or skim coat nearer 0.20 to 0.80 and tuff stone 0.50 to 1.00. The application window is +5°C to +35°C, so on a UAE site work the shaded elevation and follow the sun round rather than treating a wall that is already baking.

description: Few products on this line are bought for a single moment, but Lamposilex ME is one of them. name: Mapeband
description: A cementitious membrane cannot turn an internal corner on its own, and Mapeband is the tape that lets it. An alkali resistant rubber tape with felt edging, 0.58 mm thick and 120 mm wide, it is bedded fabric side down into a layer of Mapelastic, Mapelastic Smart, Mapelastic Turbo or Mapelastic AquaDefense at least 1 mm thick, with the membrane wetting both flanks. Ultimate elongation of at least 300 per cent and tear resistance of 100 N let a wall to floor junction move rather than split along the line, which is what an untaped junction eventually does. Over a movement joint the tape is set in an omega loop so it can be put in tension. Rolls run 50 m or 10 m, and joints between strips are sealed with Adesilex LP, not with the membrane. Service temperature reaches +60°C, enough for an exposed Dubai terrace.

name: Planiseal 88
description: An osmotic mortar works differently from a flexible coating. Planiseal 88 is a cementitious powder that seals masonry and concrete by forming crystals within the pores of the substrate itself, which is why it is suitable for contact with drinking water and classified to EN 1504-2 as MC IR. It suits stable structures such as potable water tanks and below grade walls rather than a roof or balcony that moves, because an osmotic mortar is rigid by nature. Mix 100 parts powder with 21 to 23 parts water, 5.25 to 5.75 litres per bag, allow about an hour of pot life and 1.5 kg per square metre per millimetre of thickness, from 25 kg bags. The application range reaches +40°C, generous for the Gulf, but shelf life shortens in heat and humidity, so rotate stock.

classification: CE EN 1504-2 C PI MC IR
description: Planiseal WR 100 protects reinforced concrete without covering it. A ready mixed, pure silane based hydrophobising liquid, it migrates into the surface and leaves a water repellent zone inside the concrete, so chloride bearing water is kept out while the surface keeps its appearance. That makes it a durability treatment for structures exposed to aggressive agents, chlorides in particular, which is the mechanism behind most reinforcement corrosion in coastal Gulf concrete. It goes onto vertical and horizontal surfaces, onto porous or compact concrete, onto new work and onto concrete already repaired, at roughly 0.1 to 0.2 kg per square metre per coat from 5 kg units. It is CE marked to EN 1504-2. Treat the surface once repairs have cured and the concrete is dry, because a silane needs open pores to migrate into.

name: Paviland SL 10R
description: Programme is the reason to choose the R grade. Paviland SL 10R covers the same 2 to 10 mm in one coat as Paviland SL 10 and is classified CT C25 F5, but it sets to light foot traffic in 3 to 4 hours rather than 8 to 12, can be sanded after 4 to 8 hours and takes tiles or fitted carpet from 8 to 12 hours, with subsequent bonding at 12 to 24 hours. Setting starts at 20 to 30 minutes, so the discharge area has to be planned and confined before the first bag is opened. It is pumpable, bonds above 2 N/mm2, passes 30 N/mm2 in compression and is rated for use over radiant heating. Mix 5.40 to 5.64 litres of water per 23 kg bag, interior only, between 5 and 40 degrees Celsius.

name: Paviland Primer R
description: Dilution is how this primer adapts to the floor it is given. Paviland Primer R is a dispersion primer for the absorbent cementitious substrate, which is the ordinary case under a Paviland self levelling compound, and it both seals and binds: it penetrates, hardens a dusty screed and leaves an evenly absorbent surface, so the compound above keeps its own mixing water and does not blow pinholes or bubbles. On a moderately absorbent or non-porous floor, dilute 1:1 with clean water. On a medium to highly porous one, prime twice, 1:3 first and 1:1 second, at roughly 100 and 200 g/m2 in turn, from a 10 kg jerry can. Brush, roller and airless spray all work. It dries in one to two hours on an absorbent substrate, longer on a dense one, and is rated over underfloor heating.
meta_description: Paviland Primer R dispersion bonding primer for absorbent cementitious floors before self levelling compounds. Data sheet and Dubai stock from Lapiz Blue UAE.

name: Paviland Primer Ceramic
description: A primer is chosen by what lies underneath, not by preference, and Paviland Primer Ceramic is the one for a floor that will not absorb anything: an existing ceramic or stoneware tile floor, stoneware, marble, stone, terrazzo, polished cement or very low porosity concrete. It is ready to use and must not be diluted, because the hard red film it leaves carries fine quartz aggregate that gives a cementitious levelling compound something mechanical to grip. Roll it thin and even with a medium pile roller and leave no puddles. Drying is about 90 minutes on a non-absorbent subfloor and 12 hours on calcium sulphate floors, gypsum fibre boards and sanded mastic asphalt screed. Coverage is 125 g/m2 from a 10 kg jerry can, applied between 15 and 35 degrees Celsius. Lay the levelling compound within 24 hours, while the film is still clean.

name: Paviland Primer Epoxy
description: Reach for a resin primer when there is a reason, and here the reason is moisture. Paviland Primer Epoxy is a solvent free and water free two component epoxy that penetrates deeply, strengthens a weak substrate and reduces the vapour diffusion rate on cement and concrete floors holding residual moisture of up to 5 CM per cent, which a dispersion primer cannot do. Part B is poured into Part A, 2.85 kg into 7.15 kg, and the mix has 45 minutes at 25 degrees Celsius or 30 minutes at 30. The first coat is rolled at 400 g/m2, the second at 250 g/m2 once eight to ten hours have passed, and Paviland aggregate is broadcast into that wet second coat at 2 to 2.5 kg/m2 to key the levelling compound. Apply between 15 and 35 degrees Celsius.

name: Ultrabond Eco 520
description: Linoleum behaves nothing like vinyl. A jute backed sheet needs an adhesive that grabs while it is still wet and builds legs quickly, or the roll moves as it is pressed down. Ultrabond Eco 520 is a solvent free single coat adhesive based on synthetic polymers in water dispersion, for linoleum in sheets and panels up to 4 mm thick as well as cork linoleum and corkment underlay. Waiting time is 10 to 20 minutes and open time 20 to 30 minutes, with light foot traffic after three to five hours and full service in 24 to 48 hours. Consumption is 0.30 to 0.45 kg/m² through a TKB B1, B2 or Mapei no. 2 trowel. EC1 Plus covers very low emission, and the floor is rated for castors to EN 12529. It bonds only to dry absorbent substrates, so test a UAE screed for residual damp first.

name: Ultrabond Eco 571 2K
description: Rubber backings and outdoor exposure both defeat a dispersion adhesive, and this is the grade that answers them. Ultrabond Eco 571 2K is a two component, low viscosity polyurethane adhesive free of solvent and water, mixed 86 parts A to 14 parts B, for bonding rubber tiles and sheeting with any backing, homogeneous and heterogeneous PVC, semi rigid vinyl and FRP wall panels, indoors or out, on absorbent and non absorbent substrates. Pot life is about 30 minutes, open time 40 to 50 minutes, and a covering can still be adjusted at 70 to 90 minutes, with light foot traffic after 12 to 24 hours and full set in roughly three days. description: A stair nosing or a coving cannot be weighted down while an adhesive sets, which is why detail work is bonded by contact. name: Ultrabond Eco Fast Track
description: Renovation work is sold on downtime rather than on bond strength. Ultrabond Eco Fast Track is a synthetic resin adhesive in water dispersion with a very fast initial grab, laid at approximately 200 to 400 g/m² through a Mapei 1 or 2 or a TKB A2 to B1 notch. name: Mapeflex Express 80/400
description: The name is the specification: Shore A 80 hardness with 400 per cent elongation. Mapeflex Express 80/400 is a two-component polyurea poured into horizontal joints and cracks that carry wheels, mixed one to one by volume through the static mixer on a 600 ml cartridge, so nothing is batched by hand. Speed is the reason it is bought. Hardening begins in 90 seconds, excess is sliced flat from 20 minutes, and the joint is open to traffic after 45, which lets a warehouse or car park repair finish inside one night shift. Keep it to its job: joints at least 6 mm wide, movement no more than 5 per cent of the width, falls under 4 per cent, and never in green concrete still shrinking. Application runs from 0 to 40 degrees, the full UAE working range, with tensile strength of 10 MPa and adhesion to concrete above 1 MPa.

classification: CE EN 1504-2 C PI MC IR, EN 15457 GB, EN 15458 GB
description: A render carrying hairline cracks will telegraph them through an ordinary masonry paint within a season. Elastocolor Paint is the elastomeric answer: a one-component acrylic in water dispersion that bridges micro-cracks, stays permeable to vapour while stopping liquid water, and blocks the carbon dioxide that carbonates concrete and corrodes the steel inside it. Testing to EN 15457 and EN 15458 records no growth of mould, fungi or algae, which is the reason it gets specified on shaded and humid elevations. Dilute 10 to 15 per cent with water and lay two coats over the correct primer, 12 to 24 hours apart, at 0.2 to 0.4 kg per square metre per coat. Mapei excludes it from horizontal waterproofing, immersed surfaces and anything walked on. Supplied in 20 kg drums in RAL shades, holding colour change under 2.5 delta E after 1,000 hours of accelerated weathering, which counts on a Gulf facade.
